title: Shared definitions for every contract family

relation.description: A fully qualified table name, schema-qualified. Never a vendor object id.

rounding.description: Load-bearing. Claim 5 compares consumers as integers with no tolerance, so every consumer must round identically. `decimals` fixes the integer scale: canonical_integer = round(value, decimals) * 10**decimals.

mode.description: half_even is banker's rounding (SQL bround). half_up is SQL round.

provenance.description: Doctrine rule 3 — nothing is invented. Every number that comes from outside the repository carries a citation and a verification date. A `value` without a `source` is a build failure. `kind` distinguishes a verified legal fact from a stated assumption of the synthetic scenario; both are permitted, neither may be omitted, and the two are never dressed as one another. Note the failure this cannot catch on its own: a citation that is real but does not say what the value claims. The defence against that is a `quote` long enough for a reader to check, which is why paraphrase is kept out of it.

quote.description: VERBATIM text of the cited provision, and nothing else. Ellipses may shorten it; a summary, an extract, a rubric gloss or an English paraphrase may not stand in it — those go in `note`. The quote is the only part of a citation a reviewer can check without opening the gazette, so a quote that has been helpfully tidied is worse than no quote at all.

note.description: Anything that is not the provision's own words: a summary of a long article, what an extract omits, or — importantly — the fact that this citation supports a CONTINUATION rather than a creation, which is an inference from no amending instrument having been found.

oneOf.description: A provision that was read at its source. It must carry either a verbatim `quote` — the only part of a citation a reviewer can check without opening the gazette — or a `note` accounting for why there is none. A citation with neither is an assertion with a URL attached, and the failure it hides is the worst kind: an instrument that is real and says something other than what the value claims.

note.description: What is being assumed and why. A law number may appear here, but only to DISOWN it — to record which instrument was found and why its figure is not the source of this value. What must never appear is an instrument presented as the source: that is what `kind: legal_instrument` is for, and it requires an article and a URL that can be opened.
